response.title: Which projector and screen should I buy together for about $3,000 to replace the TV in a living room that isn't dark?
response.answer:
For a $3,000 budget, I'd prioritize an ultra-short-throw (UST) laser projector paired with an ambient-light-rejecting (ALR) screen.

The screen matters almost as much as the projector in your situation. Because you're replacing a TV in a living room that isn't dark, a regular white projection screen would give you washed-out blacks and weak contrast during the day.

My target would be a 100-inch 4K laser setup, with roughly $2,000–$2,300 for the projector and $700–$1,000 for the screen.

One important caveat: even a good $3,000 projector setup won't match the daytime contrast of a modern Mini-LED TV in a bright room. The projector wins on screen size and cinematic immersion.

The two combinations I'd consider

Which would I choose?

I'd favor the PX3-PRO with a 100-inch Fresnel ALR screen if you can stretch the budget slightly. Fresnel screens can be especially useful when ambient light comes from multiple directions, though their viewing angles are more restrictive.

If $3,000 is a hard ceiling including tax, the PL2 package leaves more room in the budget.

One question that could change my recommendation

Where does most of the living room light come from?

Windows on the side of the room
Large windows directly opposite the screen
Mostly ceiling lights and lamps
Lots of daylight from multiple directions
Refine my recommendation

This matters because a screen that performs well under ceiling lights may not perform equally well with daylight hitting it from the front.
